title: What they said at the time

clips.q: Kozmo.com provides something the Web has so far lacked: instant gratification.
clips.who: **Jim Williamson**, analyst, IDC, in Forbes, Jun 22, 2000[^16]

clips.q: The current business model, selling low-margin goods and delivering them for free, is not viable for the long term.
clips.who: **Rebecca Nidositko**, Yankee Group, in Forbes, Jun 22, 2000[^16]

clips.q: Each time a Kozmo deliveryman leaves the warehouse, he has to be carrying multiple packages.
clips.who: **Ken Cassar**, Jupiter Communications, in CNET News, Feb 29, 2000[^18]

clips.q: All of a sudden, it was like waking up from a bad drunk.
clips.who: **Skip Trevathan**, Kozmo chief operating officer, on the market, Computerworld, Jan 1, 2001[^12]

clips.q: Some decisions made early in the company’s development combined with current market conditions prevented Kozmo from overcoming the challenges associated with conquering the last mile.
clips.who: **Gerry Burdo**, closing statement, Apr 11, 2001, as quoted by CNNfn[^3]

clips.q: This seemed like a dumb idea from the beginning.
clips.who: **Vern Keenan**, Keenan Vision, in CNET News, Apr 11, 2001[^4]
**Mark Leitner**, Kozmo vendor relations manager in Los Angeles, in The Globe and Mail, Apr 13, 2001[^5]

clips.q: It was fun, but I always knew it was a matter of time.
clips.who: **Doug Boag**, a New York customer, in The Globe and Mail, Apr 13, 2001[^5]

clips.q: Someone ordered a pack of Mentos. Then two hours later they’d order a pint of ice cream.
